stem:
Nandini draws two lines that cross at one point. Each of the four angles at the crossing measures $90^{\circ}$.

Which statements are correct?

statements.text: The lines are perpendicular, because four right angles at a crossing mean the lines meet at right angles.
The lines are perpendicular even when they stay apart and never meet.
The conclusion is only the label right angle, with no claim about the lines.

teacher.key_rationale: Four equal 90° angles at a meeting make the lines perpendicular. Dropping the meet condition or stopping at the right-angle label alone both miss that conclusion.
